tasks.title: Three rulings the attempt model needs (A2)
tasks.detail: The A2 survey hit three cases the spec does not cover. Answer in the note; A2's build reads them. (1) THE PEEK — tapping the grey ? on a sum reveals the answer and the round goes inert; she never answers. Is that no attempt at all, an attempt excluded like help, or an incorrect one? It decides whether a peeked stage reads as unpractised or as fine. (2) IS 'SAY IT AGAIN' HELP? The spec names dot-hints and Fred-talk only. If repeating the prompt is not help, find pages — which have no other affordance — are never help-excluded at all. (3) ABANDONMENT — she taps the X mid-page. tasks.title: The other half of JT-008(3): what does a paused page PAY?
tasks.detail: Your ruling said an abandoned challenge is paused and answers made so far count towards proficiency AND the reward progress. The proficiency half is built (A2): every word she answered was recorded as it landed, and only the unfinished one is dropped. The reward half is not, because it cannot be decided without you. THE GAP, exactly. Reading pays by the PAGE, not by the word: challengePassed adds one item to readProgress when a page completes. Build and sum pages are one question each, so leaving after answering already collects (A1 kept that deliberately). A FIND page is 3 words at first and grows to 12 - so a girl who finds 11 of 12 and taps the X banks nothing at all toward the egg. That single case is the whole of the gap. Three ways it could go, and they cost very different things. (a) PRO-RATA: pay 11/12 of a page. Needs part-items in a currency A7 just re-based to whole ones, and it moves pages-per-egg, which the month-walk pins. (b) RESUME - your word was paused: the same page comes back with the 11 words still found, she finds the twelfth, the page pays in full. Nothing in the economy moves. Costs in-session round state and a change to the ported wordFind renderer, which is a parity question rather than a free one. (c) NOTHING CHANGES: readHeld already brings the same card back, so she re-reads 11 words she can already read - which is not a punishment so much as a chore. Answer in the note and the build reads it, exactly as JT-008 did.

tasks.title: Three rulings the harness needs (A3) — how much of each thing she gets
tasks.detail: The A3 survey found one thing the spec does not cover, and it turns out to be the same question twice. The harness is keyed by PATH - levelFor('sums'), levelFor('reading') - but the island has only TWO ways into a challenge and each of them covers two paths: tapping a plot could be sums or takingAway, tapping the egg could be reading (find a word) or building (make one from letters). So before the harness can pick a STAGE, something has to pick the PATH, and that is the knob that decides what she actually plays. The reading half already has an answer sitting in balance.json that nobody chose; the maths half has no answer anywhere, because taking-away has never once been dealt on the island. Worth knowing before you answer: subtraction is entirely BUILT - the generator is ported with all three levels, the sum page already paints the minus sign and marks it correctly. Nothing is missing but the choice. Full reasoning in docs/pet-island-runA.md, FIELD NOTES - A3. (1) HOW MUCH TAKING-AWAY? You hand-tick takingAway 1 next to sums 1 (that is JT-007). What share of her maths is then take-aways? The spec says draw evenly across every ticked stage, which gives a half - but the share then DRIFTS as a side effect of unrelated ticks: the day you tick sums 2 as well, subtraction quietly drops from a half to a third, because it is one stage in three rather than one in two. The alternative is a fixed ratio in balance.json, the way reading already has one, which holds still no matter what else you tick. (2) THE READING MIX - this is PB-038 and A3 forces it open, because A3 rebuilds the very line the bug lives on. balance.json says find, build, build, build - one find page in four. Since A7 re-based the currency she has actually been getting one in two. Nobody chose either. Which do you want: one find in four as written, one in two as played, or something else? (3) CAN A PARENT EMPTY A PATH? Untick every maths stage and tapping a plot has nothing to deal; untick reading AND building and the egg can never hatch. Two ways: refuse the last untick (the panel simply will not let you), or allow it and have the island quietly stop offering that kind of round - no error, no child-facing anything, the egg just sits there. The second is more honest to 'untick is a parent's hand, not a demotion'; the first cannot be walked into by accident. Answer in the note and the build reads it, exactly as JT-008 and JT-009 did.

tasks.title: What does Manual mean once you have used it? (A4, and it shapes Run B)
tasks.detail: The panel is built and JT-007 is ready to do. The route is: grown-ups, What she is working on, Taking away, Manual, tick 'to ten'. Nothing else is needed and subtraction is hers that evening. But the mode you switch to in order to tick is a PERSISTENT, per-path setting, and the spec says Auto is the only thing that ever ticks by itself: 'Auto only ever ticks (Run B); Manual may tick or untick any built stage; Hold pins.' Read literally - which is how it is built - the path you hand-tick stays on Manual until you move it back, and Run B's automatic progression will therefore never promote taking-away for you. The one path you cared about enough to reach in by hand becomes the one path the ladder ignores. That may be exactly right: it is your hand, and a parent who reaches in has said something. It is flagged because it is invisible at the moment you do it - the panel offers no warning, and the consequence only shows up weeks later as a rung she never gets offered. Three ways to answer. (a) LEAVE IT: Manual persists, Run B skips manual paths, and moving back to Auto is a thing you do deliberately when you are done experimenting. (b) SNAP BACK: the mode returns to Auto when you close the panel, so Manual is a verb rather than a state and your ticks stand on their own. (c) MANUAL IS ADDITIVE: your ticks stand and Auto may still tick MORE on top, so hand-ticking never costs her the ladder; Hold remains the way to say stop. Built as (a) because that is the spec's own words; the other two are one predicate each in the harness. Answer in the note.

tasks.title: Is a governor an invitation or a stop? (PB-042 — you found this one)
tasks.detail: Your words, 28 July: "there is currently a hard bound. if there are not enough tiles for the number of animals, it says 'they need more homes' and wont let you do an egg. same probably applies the other way round." You are right, and it does apply both ways. THE GAP. governors.ts says of itself: "They are INVITATIONS, never lockouts. Nothing greys out; Fred asks for the other thing instead, and the child may ignore him." The first half is true. The second is not: on a paused egg tap, and on a paused socket tap, the code says Fred's line and returns without opening the round. So nothing greys out, she can tap forever, nothing she has earned is touched - and she still cannot do the thing she asked for. 'The child may ignore him' is exactly what she cannot do. WHY IT IS WORTH YOUR TIME rather than mine. Brief 19 is the rule this whole project bends to: invitations never lockouts, nothing expires, nothing taken back. A doctrine comment that misdescribes its own code is how a future change gets waved through by a rule the code does not actually follow - and this one has been sitting there being quoted. It is also a question about Juno rather than about software, which is why it is yours: a six-year-old who is told 'they need homes first' and then finds the egg simply will not open has been refused, however warm the voice. PB-039 does NOT fix this. It moves WHEN the stop fires - the maths end goes from about 1.2 tiles per animal out to your 3 animals per 2 tiles, so she meets it far less often - and leaves the mechanism exactly as it is. THREE WAYS, and (a) and (b) are opposite answers to the same sentence so nothing gets built until you pick. (a) CODE MATCHES DOCTRINE: Fred asks, and if she taps again the round opens anyway. The ask becomes real and she may override it. Softest and truest to brief 19; the risk is that the corridor stops corridoring and she banks ten animals with nowhere to put them. (b) DOCTRINE MATCHES CODE: keep the hard stop and rewrite the comment to say so plainly. A bound a child cannot cross is a perfectly good design - it just is not an invitation, and the file should stop claiming it is. (c) SPLIT THEM: the ratio corridor is a genuine stop, the break-watch stays an invitation, and the doctrine names the two kinds separately. Answer in the note.

tasks.title: "A buffer to 2:3 either way" - is it 1.5 and 3.0 tiles per pet? (PB-042)
tasks.detail: BUILT AND LIVE ALREADY - nod or reverse. Your phrase needed pinning as two numbers before anything could be coded, because 2:3 either side of a 1:2 target is not symmetric in tiles-per-pet and the two walls had to be written out. THE READINGS. (i) Symmetric in ANIMALS PER TILE: walls at 2:3 (1.5 tiles per pet, crowded) and 1:3 (3.0 tiles per pet, empty). Your 1:2 target sits at the exact midpoint, because 2/3, 1/2 and 1/3 are evenly spaced. (ii) Symmetric in TILES PER PET: 1.5 and 2.5 - but 2.5 is "two animals per five tiles", a ratio nobody says out loud, and it throws away the 2:3 you actually wrote. (iii) Multiplicative, x2/3 and x3/2: 1.333 and 3.0, which abandons 2:3 entirely. WHAT FABLE CHOSE: (i). Animals-per-tile is the unit YOU stated the target in ("1 animal per 2 tiles"), both walls are ratios a person can say aloud, and that is the house style governors.ts already sets for itself. THE CONSEQUENCE YOU SHOULD WEIGH: the empty wall at 3.0 is WIDE. At ten pets she may build thirty fields before land starts getting dear, where the old code refused her at nineteen. That is deliberate - "let the user run with whatever they want to do" - but it is the single biggest behavioural change in the card, and if it feels too loose in play the crowded wall is not the thing to move, the empty one is. WHAT IS BUILT ON IT: activeGovernor fires on these walls, and so does the price. TO REVERSE: commit bdc9290, and it is a data edit - corridor.crowded and corridor.empty in src/island/balance/balance.json.

tasks.title: Is "really really tough" +25% a step, capped at treble? (PB-042)

tasks.title: The override is a second tap, and Fred asks again every time - right? (PB-042)
tasks.detail: BUILT, SHIPPED AND ON THE LIVE SITE - this is the half Juno was stuck on, so it went out ahead of the rest. Your JT-012 note said "it should start with invitation first, then let the user run with whatever they want to do". THE QUESTION was how she says no. THE DECISION: the first tap on a paused egg or socket spends itself on Fred's line; the very next tap on the SAME thing opens the round regardless. That is option (a) exactly as the card wrote it. THE LOAD-BEARING HALF is that Fred's memory clears ON the override, so the sequence is ask, override, ask, override - every override costs one extra tap and every one of them is preceded by the announcement. A memory that persisted would mean she is asked once in a session and then silently waved through forever after, which is the silent tax again. Fred says nothing on the override itself, because the round is about to speak its own prompt and speech cancels speech. THE COST, honestly: she pays one extra tap every time she wants to overrule him. The alternative - override on the first tap - is fewer taps but no announcement at all. tasks.title: NEEDS JOE: reading just got dearer for a girl playing at one tile per animal (PB-042)
tasks.detail: NOTHING IS BUILT ON THIS ONE - it is a consequence of your numbers that you should see before Juno does. THE FACT: the new corridor runs from 1.5 to 3.0 tiles per pet. Today's effective free zone ran from about 0.667 up to about 1.5 plus a bit. The new corridor therefore sits ENTIRELY ABOVE the old one. A girl playing at a comfortable one tile per animal - which is where the old code let her sit happily - is, under the new numbers, permanently past the crowded wall and paying surcharged EGGS. So the change she will actually feel is not "the stop became a price". It is "reading got more expensive unless I build more land". WHY THAT MIGHT BE EXACTLY RIGHT: it is the pedagogy pushing her to do maths until the island reaches your 1:2 target, and the surcharge is capped so it never becomes a wall. WHY IT MIGHT NOT BE: she is six, reading is the half she likes, and a permanent tax on the thing she likes is a strange lever to pull. IF IT IS WRONG, the fix is not the escalation constants - it is the crowded wall itself. Dropping it from 1.5 to about 1.0 would restore roughly today's comfort zone while keeping the 1:2 target and the empty wall. That is corridor.crowded in src/island/balance/balance.json. Answer in the note.

tasks.title: Taking away is offered off sums 1 alone, before sums 2. Right rung? (PB-030)
tasks.detail: Run B's promotion gate is ewma .85, 20 attempts, 8 probes at .70, no recent rescue, 2 distinct days. Fable chose: gate the introduction on SUMS STAGE 1 alone (ewma .85, 20 attempts, no recent rescue, 2 distinct days), drop the probe clause, and offer 'takingAway 1'. If a trickier-sums offer is due the same session, taking away wins - one offer per session forces the choice. Rejected (b): deal subtraction probes before the path is open, so the probe clause CAN be met. Failure mode - she meets a minus sign nobody introduced, and the debut ritual ('the minus sign popping on debut') becomes a re-run. Rejected (c): wait until sums 2 is proficient. Failure mode - it contradicts your own JT-010 worked example, 'one easy sum, one easy sub and one medium sum, is 2/3 sum 1/3 sub', which has sub arriving ALONGSIDE sums 2 rather than queued behind it. WHAT IS BUILT ON IT: commit 1cf4e71, the whole introduction branch in src/island/harness.ts. Reversing to (c) is a one-line change to which stage the intro gate reads. Reversing to (b) is a slice. SECOND, SMALLER CALL inside the same commit, flag it if it is wrong: the introduction requires TAKING AWAY to be on Auto, but does not require SUMS to be - so a parent who put sums on Manual still gets subtraction offered, because JT-011 governs which path Auto may TICK and sums is only the witness. The opposite reading is one predicate.

tasks.title: The price starts at 1.2 and 4.0 tiles per pet, Fred still speaks at 1.5 and 3.0 (PB-042)
tasks.detail: BUILT AND LIVE ALREADY - nod or retune. You asked us to pick both numbers, so this is the answer rather than the question, but one consequence cuts across JT-018 and you should see it. THE SHAPE: Fred speaks at the corridor you ratified, 1.5 tiles per pet crowded and 3.0 empty. Nothing costs more there. The surcharge starts further out, at 1.2 and 4.0. Between the two she has been told and is not being charged, which is the daylight you asked for. HOW THE TWO NUMBERS WERE FIXED - measured over every island from 1 to 40 animals, not chosen by eye. CROWDED: standing exactly on the warning wall leaves ZERO spare animals at every pet count 1..40, so before this change the first egg after Fred spoke was always already a charged egg - the warning had no room to act in. Widening the divisor buys about one spare animal per six tiles. 1.2 is the tightest divisor that buys at least one spare animal at every size out of grace: 1.4 fails at 6, 7, 8, 10 and 12 animals, 1.3 still fails at 6 animals on 9 tiles. EMPTY: the old wall charged a step at the VERY FIRST tile past it, at every pet count 1..12. 3.5 does not fix it and nor does 3.75 - at one animal the first overshoot is 4 tiles. 4.0 is the smallest multiplier that absorbs the first overshoot at every size, and it buys exactly one spare tile per animal. THE CONSEQUENCE TO WEIGH, and it is the JT-018 one. The crowded wall prices EGGS, so moving it out from 1.5 to 1.2 makes reading CHEAPER past the wall, and you said reading should in general be more expensive because the animal stash is finite and must not run out. The size of it, measured: at eight animals on six tiles an egg falls from 44 pages to 39; at ten on eight, from 54 to 48; at ten on five, from 66 to 60. Roughly ten to fifteen per cent off, only in the band past the wall, and list price is untouched. We judged that acceptable because the escalation and the treble cap are unchanged and the empty side was left far more generous than the crowded side precisely on your reasoning - tiles are unlimited, animals are not. IF YOU WANT READING DEARER AGAIN: raise price.crowded back toward 1.5, or raise escalation.slope from 0.25. Both are single numbers in the governor block of src/island/balance/balance.json and no code moves.

tasks.title: Your grace period means Fred can never mention crowding below six animals (PB-042)
tasks.detail: BUILT AND LIVE ALREADY - nod or retune. Not a question about what you meant; a consequence of what you said that you may not have wanted. You ruled JT-016 as 'grace period up to 5 animals and 10 tiles', built as an AND: grace holds while she has at most 5 animals AND at most 10 tiles, and ends the moment either one grows. THE CONSEQUENCE. With 5 animals or fewer she can only leave grace by passing 10 tiles - and 10 tiles for 5 animals is 2.0 tiles per animal, which is exactly your target. So there is no island with 5 or fewer animals that is both out of grace and past the crowded wall. Fred's 'they need homes' line is unreachable until she has a sixth animal. The empty side is unaffected: an eleventh tile with two animals leaves grace and is genuinely bare, and Fred says so. WHETHER THAT IS RIGHT. We think it is, and built on it: the first five animals are the tutorial, a beginner should never be told she has too many friends, and the empty-side nudge still teaches her the loop. But it does mean one of the two governors is silent for the whole opening, which is more than 'up to 5 animals' obviously implies. IF YOU WANT IT OTHERWISE: making grace an OR - it ends when either number is still small - would let Fred speak to a child with 6 animals on 2 tiles sooner, but would also end grace for a child with 1 animal on 11 tiles who is plainly still learning. Dropping grace.pets to 3 would open the crowded side at 4 animals. Both are one number or one operator in src/island/balance/balance.json and src/island/balance/index.ts (graceHolds).

tasks.title: Fred now has to count out loud - twenty numerals to record (JT-019)
tasks.detail: A new recording obligation, flagged before the character pass rather than after it, because docs/pet-island-voice.md 5.0 says the premium bake happens exactly once. YOUR JT-019 RULING - 'we get fred to tell her how many she needs to restore balance' - means two of Fred's lines now have a number spliced into them: 'They need homes! 3 more tiles will do it.' The splice law (voice.md 3) forbids crossing voices inside one sentence, so the numerals must be FRED's, not the teacher's - the teacher counting inside Fred's mouth is exactly the uncanny join the law exists to stop. WHAT THAT COSTS YOU: one clip per number, registered in voice/scripts.json as the 'count.' family. WE CHOSE 1-20, and it is a judgement rather than a derived bound. Measured over every island up to sixty tiles and twenty animals, the number Fred actually asks for is 1 to 4 in ordinary play; it only passes 20 on islands a child would have to work very hard to reach, and any number with no clip falls back to the robot voice like any other missing line (voice.md 6), so overshooting is safe and undershooting is survivable. Say if you would rather record fewer - ten covers everything realistic - or more. NOTHING IS BLOCKED ON THIS: the lines are live and speaking now through Web Speech.

tasks.title: The honeymoon makes MATHS cheaper only, not reading (PB-030 B2)

tasks.title: Is "bounded 65/35" a limit on the LEAN, or a clamp on the SHARE? (PB-030 B3)
tasks.detail:
Run A specs the last piece of Run B as "weakness-lean between paths bounded 65/35 on persistent estimates only" (runA.md:236). Your JT-010(1) says "share of maths stays by tick" and your worked example is "one easy sum, one easy sub and one medium sum, is 2/3 sum 1/3 sub".

Those two collide: 2/3 is 0.667, which already exceeds the 65/35 the spec names. So the lean had to be read one of three ways.

(a) CLAMP THE SHARE. Always force the split into 35-65. Literal, but it rewrites your worked example to 0.65/0.35 even for a child with no weakness at all - i.e. it changes behaviour when the lean is doing nothing, which quietly reverses JT-010.
(b) LEAN UP TO 0.65. Zero lean leaves today alone, but at full lean a path with one tick out of three could be pushed from 0.333 to 0.65 - the estimate then overrules the tick structure you set.
(c) BOUND THE LEAN ITSELF. Multiply the weaker path weight by at most 65/35 and renormalise. Zero lean is today exactly; at the 1:1 tick shape the ladder drives toward, full lean lands on exactly 65/35 (the spec number); at your 2:1 example it lands on .519/.481 - noticeably more of the weak path, but it can never invert which path leads.

FABLE CHOSE (c), on the grounds that the spec sentence is about the "weakness-lean", not about the share, so read that way the spec and your ruling stop disagreeing - and that (c) is the only option where a tick a parent made always leads.

BUILT ON IT (commit 9138176). The lean is one multiplier. Both paths must have at least 8 answered attempts or there is no lean at all, so a freshly opened taking-away path is dealt at its tick share rather than force-fed. A dead zone of .05 stops session noise flapping the mix, and the full lean arrives at a gap of .30.

IF YOU REVERSE IT: cheap. Option (a) wraps option (c) without unwinding it - it is a clamp applied after, roughly an hour plus tests. Option (b) is a different formula in the same one function. The dials all sit in one block marked PROVISIONAL in src/island/harness.ts, in the style you asked for on JT-021, so the numbers can be tuned from play testing without touching the mechanism.

tasks.title: The kits build head and body as two shapes; every original is ONE. Do we rebuild the 72? (PB-036)
tasks.detail:
YOUR AXIOM IS CONFIRMED, AND IT IS STRUCTURAL.

You said "head = body". Measured over all 24 originals: in 0 of 24 does a head separate
from a torso. Every pack animal is one continuous shell running nose to tail. There is no
seam at the neck because there is no neck.

All three kits do the opposite. Each emits a head box and a body box as siblings, never
merged: quadruped.ts:229 and :269, raptor.ts:289 and :372, songbird.ts:205 and :268. The
head is unconditional and clamped away from zero, so it cannot even be turned off.
ALL 72 BUILT SPECIES are two shapes where every original is one.

Two more of your axioms land the same way. All 48 eyes in the pack have EXACTLY zero
thickness (48 of 48); the kits build eyes as protruding balls with a second ball in front
for the pupil. All 86 legs sit at one of six positions under the body; the kits
approximate a leg the pack already ships as a reusable buffer.

AND THE PACK IS ALREADY BUILT THE WAY YOU DESCRIBED.
The body shell is the IDENTICAL 1.250 cube in 13 of the 24 - same 60 triangles, same 120
points. Only 10 distinct body shells exist in the whole pack. Kenney made 24 animals by
assembling and adjusting a small parts vocabulary. Your instruction is not a new method,
it is his method.

WHAT IT WOULD BUY. 206 separable shells across the 24 bodies; 182 feature parts across ~25
kinds - 48 eye cards, 42 ears, 25 noses and snouts, 22 antlers/horns/ossicones/crests,
plus tails, wings and the one leg. Honest variety: ~2,100 creatures a five-year-old could
tell apart, of which ~300-600 read as a different animal. My earlier answer to you - that
24 faces was the ceiling - WAS WRONG. It assumed the head was atomic. It is atomic, but
the face is not part of it.

REACH: 186 of the 296 can be built from real parts. 64 cannot be built at all - Ocean,
Critters, Dinosaurs and Raptors, for want of a fin, an insect wing, a frill and a hooked
beak. 46 are partial (Birds, Outback, Legendary). We have invented nothing and will not.

THE COST, PLAINLY. Building your way means the 72 existing species are REBUILT, not tuned.
The species records - proportions, palette, which ears - largely survive; the kit machinery
underneath them is replaced. Nothing has been rebuilt or deleted yet.

THE OPTIONS.
A) Rebuild the kits to assemble lifted pack parts onto one fused shell. Matches the pack
   exactly. Costs a rewrite of three kits and a re-check of all 72. Caps us at 186 of 296
   until parts are found or drawn for the other four collections.
B) Keep the kits and fix only the eye (flat card, absolute size). Cheapest, closes most of
   "the eye design is inconsistent", leaves head-as-separate-box - so they still will not
   read as Kenney animals.
C) Hybrid: fuse head into body and adopt the real leg, tail and wing, but keep the shell
   procedural so all 296 stay reachable. Middle cost, and the only option that does not
   cap the roster.

FABLE WAS NOT ASKED. This changes what a child sees, so it is yours alone.

GO AND LOOK FIRST: npm run workbench, Anatomy tab (3rd). The fox comes apart into 10
labelled parts; the deer into 15 with its antlers as real separable objects. Kenney’s own
names are plain, ours are amber and say so. Full write-up in
docs/how-the-animals-are-made.md, part two.
tasks.note: ANSWERED 2 Aug 2026, and the answer is yes — rebuild them. Joe: "only the garden animals have been built to spec. the ones i can see in outline in the album for africa and home pets are the old blocky ones that can be deleted to be honest. do not build any more of them. all the rest must be built in the same way as the garden animals. which should be pretty much deterministic and quick." So the KIT ROUTE IS RETIRED for authoring: 59 kit-built species across home-pets (14), africa (13), farm (16) and woodland (16) are rejected work. He ordered them replaced BEFORE new collections are built, because those four collections are already openable and are what Juno actually sees.

tasks.title: How do the new nouns reach her — a new list, or a deliberate golden re-capture? (JT-004)
tasks.detail:
joe/noun-candidates.json now exists (88 clean 3- and 4-letter nouns, 23 flagged, 35 rejected). It was never written before, which is why JT-004 has sat open: your red pen had nothing to red-pen. Strike what you do not want by setting each verdict to "no"; empty means unreviewed.

The blocker is structural, not editorial. The live list is GREEN in src/core/wordlists.ts:17, and it cannot be appended to. Three things break at once: makeDeck deals straight from the array so its order is load-bearing (wordlists.ts:4); tools/golden/capture.mjs:37 pins the v0 word arrays as literals; and src/core/alien.ts:25 spreads GREEN into REAL_BLOCK, so one extra word shifts the rng stream feeding read, readL2 AND build. Adding a single noun to GREEN reddens the frozen golden.

Option (a): ship the approved nouns as a NEW list dealt by a new reading rung of its own. golden.json is untouched and stays a true regression gate. It matches the note already in harness.ts:53 — a future reading rung is a new generator, not a new number. More code, and reading gets a real second rung, which is the thing JT-024 says the honeymoon offer is currently lying about.

Option (b): append to GREEN and deliberately re-capture golden (npm run golden:capture), stating it in the commit. Much less code. The cost is that the frozen baseline for reading, word-building and the alien blocklist is re-cut, so any generator drift that existed before this run becomes invisible — the gate can no longer tell us the old behaviour survived.

Nothing has been built on either option. No noun is live and no child sees any of this today; only the candidate file and the maths rung shipped this run (521b744, 1a8fef5). Choosing (a) costs nothing already written. Choosing (b) would mean a separate, stated re-capture commit — never as a side effect of a feature.

Related: JT-005 (pairs audit) promises joe/pairs-audit.json, which also does not exist yet. Same shape of question when it lands, so a ruling here likely settles that one too.

tasks.title: NEEDS JOE: our animals carry almost nothing above the body cube — do four of them get ears? (PB-036)
tasks.detail:
Your size note is fixed, but measuring it turned up a second, separate thing that is yours to call.

YOUR NOTE: "the new animals look genuinely really good. general criticism is size. the body/cube should always be the standard size, its often bigger."

WHAT WAS ACTUALLY WRONG, measured over all 14 Garden species and all 24 originals:
1. The geometry was already right. Every built hull is exactly 1.250 on x and y (1.125 on z for the three that use a different real shell). No node carries a scale. No species stretched its hull. The badger’s 1.539 is the box-12 shell’s own ear lugs with the torso still exactly 1.250.
2. The BUILDER let it happen anyway — hull.stretch multiplied the cube by any number at all, guarded only by a prose sentence. That is now a type error and a build-time throw (b5afc00), and the harness asserts every species’ hull against its shell’s own size. This is the second time you raised it; the first fix was for the hedgehog alone, which is why it came back.
3. The thing you were actually LOOKING at was the viewer. It divided every animal by its OWN height, so an identical 1.250 cube drew at 0.87 of the frame for the 1.431-tall mouse and 0.63 for the 1.976-tall squirrel — a 1.38x swing in apparent body size, invented by the review tool, and applied to the pack animal beside it too. Both halves now share one scale (60666d2), so the cube is the same size on screen for all fourteen. Nothing about the animals changed.

THE QUESTION THIS LEFT. Kenney gets an animal’s height from what sits ON TOP of the cube — ears in 9 of 24, horns or antlers in 3, a crest or tuft in 3, a raised tail in 4. Mean clearance above the hull top: 0.236. Ours is 0.134, and four species have exactly 0.000 — the MOUSE, SHREW, MOLE and BADGER, whose cube IS the top of the animal. All four therefore sit on the height floor (1.43125, the height of a bare cube on standard legs) and give the cube 87.3% of their silhouette, against the pack’s median 77.6%. Our legs are the pack’s own 0.18125 to the digit, so it is not the legs.

So even at honest scale those four read blockier than a Kenney animal. Three options:
A) Give each of the four something honest above the hull — real ears for the mouse, shrew and badger, and for the mole either a low crest or nothing, since a mole genuinely has almost no ear. Cost: four species rebuilt, four fingerprints repinned, no budget risk (adding parts only adds vertices, and it lifts all four off the height floor).
B) Let those four swap to the pack’s own taller shell, box-21 (1.250 x 1.5051 x 1.250). The fox does exactly this and is the most cube-dominant original at 0.893. Cost: one line each, but it makes the body taller rather than adding an animal feature, and none of our fourteen uses box-21 today.
C) Leave them. A mole and a shrew genuinely are blunt little animals, and the elephant is a real Kenney model with 0.000 above its hull too.

NOTHING HAS BEEN BUILT ON ANY OF THESE. I did not choose, because ear-or-no-ear on four animals is a look, not a measurement, and looks are yours. Fable was not asked for the same reason. Nothing needs reverting whichever way you go; the harness invariant added this run is about hull SIZE and is unaffected.

If you pick A, say for each of the four whether it gets ears — the mole is the one I would expect you to answer differently.

tasks.title: NEEDS JOE: does your Sassoon licence let us put the font in a PUBLIC repo? (PB-051)
tasks.detail:
PB-051 is BUILT and GREEN but is NOT on main, and will not be until you answer this. The work sits on branch `pb-051-sassoon-font` (81af67f, f0f36b8) with its handoff at docs/handoffs/PB-051.md. Nothing is lost either way.

WHY IT STOPPED. github.com/jtr31415/JunosIsland is PUBLIC. Sassoon Infant is commercial — the zip's own COPYRIGHT.txt says "This product is licensed, not sold, and may only be used in accordance with the terms specified in the License Agreement" — and that License Agreement is not in the zip, so nothing on disk says what you are permitted to do. Committing the .ttf to a public repo is redistribution, not use.

THE DETAIL THAT DECIDED IT. .gitignore:16 already excludes Assets/*.zip, so the font has NEVER been in the repo. Somebody — you — already drew this line for source assets. Merging would be the first time Sassoon binaries entered public git history, and git history is the part that is genuinely hard to undo: deleting the file later does not remove it from the history that has been cloned.

WHAT IS NEEDED FROM YOU, one of:
A) Your licence permits webfont embedding and redistribution — say so, and it merges as built.
B) It does not, or you cannot find the agreement — then the retreat is three edits and is written down in the handoff. Options are to keep the font out of git and load it from a path you place by hand, or to ship a free teaching-hand face (Andika and Edu QLD Beginner are open-licensed and have the single-storey a and open-tailed g that make Sassoon the right choice for a child learning to read).
C) You want to buy a licence tier that covers it — then this waits on that.

WHAT IS TRUE REGARDLESS. The build itself is sound and all five gates are green (2712 tests, smoke 8/8, parity 18/18). It found a surface CSS could never have reached: src/island/sign.ts paints "Juno's Island" into a canvas texture and had been out of step with the app's font since it was built. It also had to add .gitattributes, because `* text=auto eol=lf` would have silently corrupted the glyph tables, and to teach the island's precache glob about .ttf — without which the font would have worked online and vanished offline with every test still green.

ALSO WORTH YOUR EYE, once it merges: a screenshot of the old face beside the new one. The handoff says how to get both builds.
tasks.note: ANSWERED 2 Aug 2026 by dismissing the font, not by resolving the licence: "lets dismiss the sassoon idea and we keep fonts as they are." No licence was ever produced, so the question is closed as moot rather than settled. Fonts stay Edu SA Beginner + Andika (OFL-1.1).

Reversible in one function, `groupShapes`. Say which you want, or say 'try role and I will look'.

tasks.title: NEEDS JOE: five questions off the asset-loading survey (PB-048)
tasks.detail:
You asked for investigation and discussion first, so nothing was built. The survey is docs/asset-loading-survey.md, measured against a real build. Three things you did not know before answering:

1. THE SCALE PROBLEM IS ALREADY SOLVED, and the kits solved it. A Kenney GLB costs ~141 KB per species, so 296 of them would be ~41.7 MB. A parts-bank definition costs ~9.9 KB of source, so 296 are ~2.9 MB — roughly fourteenfold better, and it compresses far better again because it is repetitive source rather than binary geometry. Nothing about loading needs to change to make the roster fit.

2. THE REAL ISSUE IS EAGER PARSING, NOT SIZE. All of it compiles into ONE JS chunk (297 KB gzipped today), so every species she has never unlocked is parsed at boot — and your own JT-027 rule caps her at four open collections. The splitting seam already exists and is the same unit she unlocks: a collection.

3. THERE IS NO AUDIO AT ALL. Your card says 'given all the audio, flora and fauna', but not one sound file ships — speech is synthesised through Azure at runtime and the 43 phonemes are still JT-006. So audio is a future weight whose shape is entirely in your gift, which is why question 4 is worth answering now rather than after the recordings exist.

AND ONE THING THE CARD DID NOT ASK ABOUT, which may be the most important line in the survey: THE GAME DOES NOT WORK OFFLINE. vite.island.config.ts:69 precaches only js/css/html/woff2 and there is no runtimeCaching at all — 8 precache entries, not one 3D model among them. On a tablet with no connection the app boots to a shell and then cannot load a single animal, tile, tree or mountain. Whether that matters is question 3.

THE FIVE QUESTIONS, each answerable in a sentence:
(1) Does an unopened collection ship to the device at all? Splitting trades a smaller boot for a wait at the moment an album opens — and that moment is a reward, so a spinner on it is a real cost.
(2) Is a longer first boot acceptable in exchange for no waiting later? Suits a tablet set up once by an adult and then handed over.
(3) Do you expect her to play with no connection? This decides whether the offline finding is a defect or a non-issue.
(4) When the recorded voice arrives, does it ship with the app or stream? Phonemes are small, numerous and needed with low latency — a different problem from one big model.
(5) Is there a device you are actually targeting? One named device turns most of these from opinions into measurements.

NOTHING IS BUILT AND NOTHING SHOULD BE until (3) is answered, because offline support and lazy-loading pull in opposite directions and building either first makes the other dearer.

tasks.title: Does the lion's tail read as a goldfish's fin? (PB-036)
tasks.detail: The goldfish is built and Home Pets is now 16 of 16. Everything on it is the pack's own fish — box-20 is the hull the fish donated, box-19 is the fish's own shell-ring worn upright as a dorsal and ventral fin, plate-08 is the fish's round eye and plate-03 its mouth card. One part is NOT: the tail. The bank has no fin, no flipper and no fluke at all — that is measured, and docs/how-the-animals-are-made.md section 14 names the same absence as the reason the whole Ocean collection cannot be built. So the caudal fin is wedge-15, the LION's tail, and it is the only one of the pack's seven tails nothing else had spent. Numerically it is a good fit: 0.280 across, 1.0824 tall, 0.5552 long, tapering to half along its length, mounted at the body's own centre pointing straight back — a thin vertical blade, which is the right shape. Whether it READS as a goldfish's fan at tablet distance is a look, and looks are yours. FABLE WAS NOT ASKED, deliberately: the orders say a decision that changes what a child sees is not Fable's to settle. NOTHING ELSE DEPENDS ON THIS. If you say no, the fallback is not another shape, because there is not one — it is either authored geometry under rule 1's escape clause (which you have invoked exactly once, for the hedgehog's nose) or the goldfish keeps a stub tail and finds its 114 vertices somewhere else, since rule 9's VERTEX floor is what that part is really carrying. Reversing it changes one commit, the feat(PB-036) that added animal-goldfish.ts, and no other species. Two other things on these two animals are also unreviewed and are called out in their own flags: both palettes (neither species was ever in its collection file to be given colours) and the crocodile's deliberate absence of teeth, which brief 19's 'bright, never scary' is the reason for. tasks.title: ANSWERED: hooves are a two-tone leg, not a part (PB-074 Farm)
tasks.detail: Farm has five hooved species (horse, donkey, ox, mule, water buffalo) plus pony in Home Pets, and "hoof" occurs zero times in the parts bank. Under JT-041 nobody may author one. Joe: "just use a two tone leg for hooves". The mechanism already exists and needs no new code: CreatureDef.legs already takes a paint, and Paint.patch is { below, at } — the base slot cell is drawn as two colours and the part vertices read across it by their own height, so the line falls wherever the image says and NO triangle edge and NO geometry are needed. A hooved species is therefore one line, roughly legs: { paint: { base: "limb", patch: { below: "hoof", at: 0.25 } } }. Three real constraints: (1) at is a fraction of the part own height and must sit on the pack 1/16 grid, so 0.125, 0.1875 or 0.25 — texture.ts refuses anything else, and a horse hoof is a shallower band than an ox fetlock; (2) the patch applies to the BASE slot only, so a triangle byBand has already sent elsewhere keeps its flat colour — do not combine the two; (3) spin a patched part and the boundary spins with it, which is safe today because legs are not spun but is a trap for anything patched later. SECOND-ORDER, and the reason this is worth recording as a general tool rather than a hoof workaround: the same one line is fur socks, pale paws, a bird feet against its legs, a dark-stockinged fawn. Several Home Pets and Farm species want it for reasons that have nothing to do with hooves.
tasks.note: Just use a two tone leg for hooves.

tasks.title: Juno still owns a pet called Defuck. Do we rename it in her save? (PB-076)
tasks.detail:
THE FIX THAT SHIPPED. The hatch no longer draws a random name; a new friend now takes its species' frozen, screened name (the bunny is Chudup). Measured: the old unseeded draw could produce 640 distinct obscene names, one hatch in 678, because src/core/names.ts blocks shit/cock/dick/piss/arse but not fuck or cunt. All 320 allocated names screen clean, and tests/island/name-screen.test.ts now fails loudly if that ever stops being true. Commits 69eb970 and 075c565.

WHAT IT DOES NOT DO. The fix is FORWARD-ONLY. A pet already in a save keeps the name it was born with: save.ts reads pets back verbatim, and every display path reads pet.name off the stored record rather than deriving it from the species. Pet.id embeds the name too (pet3-Defuck). So if the Defuck rabbit is still on Juno's island, IT IS STILL CALLED THAT, and no amount of further naming work changes that by itself.

THE QUESTION, and it is yours because it changes what a child experiences: do you want her existing pet renamed in place? Options. (a) DO NOTHING - it is one pet, she may have forgotten it, and any rewrite of a save is a risk to the thing brief 19 protects. (b) RENAME IN PLACE - a one-off migration that rewrites pet.name and pet.id for any stored pet whose name fails the screen, keeping the pet, its species, its position and its place in the album. The pet is never lost, replaced or re-hatched. This is buildable and testable but it is the only code in the project that would ever edit a name a child already owns, and that is precisely the thing naming.ts was written to forbid. Nothing has been built on either option yet - this is genuinely open.

A SECOND, SMALLER THING while you are here. A name is now per SPECIES, not per pet, which is what roster section 3 asked for. The deck deals without replacement for the first 24 pets, so nothing changes until a child owns 25; after that two pets of one species carry one name (the album already routes the duplicate to More friends, and pet ids stay unique, so nothing breaks - it just reads oddly). JT-027 says a new collection opens at 80 percent, which pushes this further out, and JT-029 already suggests the fix in your own words: add something like 'the great' to their original name. Say the word and that becomes a card; it is not built.
